chunks: Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah narrated from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام that he said:
The extravagant person has three signs: he eats what does not belong to him, buys what does not belong to him, and wears what does not belong to him.

key_terms.ثَلَاثُ: three; indicating the number of defining signs mentioned
key_terms.لِلْمُسْرِفِ: for the extravagant person; one given to excess and overstepping proper bounds
key_terms.مَا لَيْسَ لَهُ: what is not his; that over which he has no rightful claim or ownership
key_terms.يَأْكُلُ: he eats; consumes or partakes of
key_terms.يَلْبَسُ: he wears; puts on as clothing

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of an extravagant person in the hadith of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith identifies extravagance through conduct that exceeds rightful limits and involves taking or using what one has no right to. It presents israf not merely as excess in spending, but as a moral failure tied to violating rightful ownership and proper restraint.
